document.description: ManX is the soluble and peripheral inner-membrane EIIAB phosphotransfer subunit of the mannose-family PTS in Escherichia coli K-12. Its N-terminal EIIA domain receives phosphate from HPr at His10; its C-terminal EIIB domain carries His175 and transfers phosphate to incoming sugar in the assembled ManXYZ transporter. Phosphotransfer occurs both within one polypeptide and between subunits of the ManX homodimer. ManY and ManZ provide the membrane translocation machinery. The complex imports and phosphorylates mannose and also accepts glucose, fructose and amino sugars. Sugar taxis is an additional system-level context; lambda DNA penetration is mediated by the membrane components and does not require ManX.

review.summary: ManX catalyses histidyl-phosphate transfer during coupled import of mannose and other supported sugars.
review.reason: The broad phosphotransfer claim is sound, not an over-annotation merely because ManX is not an ATP-dependent kinase. Its EIIB His175 directly donates phosphate to transported sugar with the membrane partners present (PMID:2681202). Refine to the existing mannose PTS activity. GO:0022870 is a verified descendant of this general function. The catalytic assignment does not claim isolated ManX transports sugar across a bilayer. PAINT lineage inspection found no IRD/IKR blocking this target; the more precise target chemistry does not challenge the conserved ancestral phosphotransfer function. The refinement retains all four substrate contexts already supported in this review: mannose, glucose, fructose and N-acetylglucosamine. Current GO glucose/fructose PTS definitions do not specify a phosphate position; GO:0022880 does require GlcNAc6-phosphate, independently documented in PMID:9864311 Figure1. This is biochemical/pathway synthesis rather than claiming the 2019 ManYZ counterflow assay measured every coupled reaction. The core records contribution to assembled transport, preserving the direct ManX catalytic role.

ManX (IIIMan, 35 kDa) is a hydrophilic protein that is transiently phosphorylated and contains the active site for sugar phosphorylation. document.description: ManL is the fused IIA/IIB phosphorelay component of the ManLMN sugar phosphotransferase system in Streptococcus mutans UA159. Its two cytoplasmic domains relay phosphate from HPr to sugar during uptake through the ManM/ManN membrane machinery. The system transports mannose and glucose and contributes to amino-sugar uptake. ManL also influences carbohydrate catabolite repression, although the direct regulatory mechanism is incompletely resolved. Alternative mannose uptake can compensate for loss of ManL, so ManLMN is not the only native route under every growth condition.
